context: A 5-stage scrollytelling network diagram showing how a synthetic community grows from 5 founders to 65 nodes across progressive scroll steps, with a sticky force-layout on the right and narrative text on the left.
first_impression: Clean and well-paced — the scrollytelling format is the right tool here, progressive disclosure prevents the full 65-node hairball from ever landing without narrative scaffolding.
what_works: Stage-by-stage reveal eliminates cognitive overload that would hit immediately in a static full-network view; the colorblind-safe TOL palette is restrained and the per-stage annotation layer (dashed circles, diamond markers, leader lines) tells viewers exactly where to look without adding new visual variables.
what_doesnt: The legend lists a single 'Community' entry (green) but at Stage 3 the three communities render in three distinct colors — Design (green), Engineering (yellow), Research (purple) — leaving two colors unaccounted for in the legend; a viewer without the in-chart text labels would be confused. Additionally, the simulation reheats to alpha=0.6 on every scroll step, so previously-settled nodes jump and re-settle, breaking object constancy for nodes that persist across stages — perceptual evaluation of this is limited from a static screenshot of Stage 1.
